title: Coffee Berry Borer: How to Spot It and Protect Your Beans
metaTitle: Coffee Berry Borer: Signs, Damage and Control
metaDescription: The coffee berry borer breeds inside coffee beans and spoils quality. Learn the signs and the picking, stripping and Beauveria steps that cut its numbers.
excerpt: The coffee berry borer, Hypothenemus hampei, is a tiny black beetle that bores into coffee berries and breeds inside the bean. Even a light attack lowers the quality and the price of your coffee. This page shows how to spot it and how to break its life cycle.

heroImage.alt: Tiny shiny black Hypothenemus beetles, the genus of the coffee berry borer, on a berry they have bored into
heroImage.credit: L. Shyamal, CC BY SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text:
The adult female is only about 1.5 to 1.9 mm long and black, covered in short stiff hairs. A female flies to ripening berries and bores a hole in one. Males have reduced wings and stay inside the berry. Females far outnumber males, and studies give ratios from 5 to 1 up to hundreds to 1.

The beetle lives worldwide, in Asia, Africa, the Americas and Oceania. Because it breeds inside the bean, spray does not reach it easily. Cultural work at harvest is the main tool for the Filipino coffee farmer. DOST PCAARRD names the berry borer, with coffee leaf rust, as the problem that has hampered coffee production the most in the country.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: It attacks ripening berries, and it survives between seasons in old berries left on the tree and on the ground.

The fertilized female bores into a ripening berry and lays eggs inside the bean over several weeks. Pacific Pests gives 30 to 50 eggs, and a review of the global pest says a female can lay more than 100. Development takes about 4 weeks, and females fly to new berries, sometimes carried far by air currents.

blocks.text: How to Identify Coffee Berry Borer

Look at the berries for a small round hole with brown frass around it. Cut open some berries and look for the tiny black beetles, white grubs or damaged beans. Check the fallen and dried berries on the ground too, because that is where the beetles wait for the next crop. Berry drop from other causes shows no entry hole.

items: A small round entry hole shows on the berry, with brown frass over it.
Berries drop early after decay organisms enter the hole.
Beans inside are partly or fully eaten.
Tiny black beetles and white grubs live inside the bean.
Dried berries left on the tree or on the ground hold live beetles.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Berries that drop from drought or from [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose) show no entry hole. A round hole with brown frass points to the borer.
How Coffee Berry Borer Hurts Your Crop

Even a small attack lowers bean quality and makes the coffee harder to sell. The beetle can attack up to all of the berries in a badly infested field. Damage plus decay organisms cause early berry drop.

Because one beetle starts a colony inside the bean, it takes only a few weeks for the numbers to rise. Compare it with the pests of other trees, such as the [cacao pod borer](/pests/cacao-pod-borer), which also hides inside the fruit. Clean and frequent harvest mostly controls it. Kerala Agricultural University says heavy attacks on robusta affected 30 to 80 percent of the berries.
How to Control Coffee Berry Borer

items: Pick the berries as they ripen. In affected areas, harvest early in the season every 2 to 3 weeks.
Collect fallen and blackened berries from the ground and destroy them, so the beetles have nowhere to wait.

After the main harvest, strip every berry from the tree, green, ripe, over ripe and dried, for about 3 months to break the life cycle. A review of the global pest calls strip picking the most important part of integrated management. Leave no old berries on the tree.
Keep the trees healthy with proper fertilizing and pruning, since a healthy tree gives clean berries.

Use the fungus Beauveria bassiana, but expect a mixed result. The Pacific fact sheet reports about 80 percent of adults killed in high humidity places, while a global review gives field results from under 1 percent to about 70 percent. It works best early in the season when females are boring in.

Protect or release the parasitoid wasps Prorops nasuta, Phymastichus coffea and Cephalonomia stephanoderis where they are available, but their effect is limited, and Prorops needed many releases in one review.
Trap the adults. A study in Atok, Benguet caught the most beetles with 4 lure traps per 50 coffee trees, set during the months when few berries are on the trees.

blocks.text: The Pacific fact sheet recommends a spray only when monitoring shows more than 2 percent of berries infested. The global review suggests a threshold between 1.5 and 2.5 percent. It must go on early. Once the female enters the bean, a spray does little. Follow the label and the FPA registration.

blocks.caption: Active ingredients that work. Always follow the label of an FPA registered product.
rows: when monitoring shows more than 2 percent infested berries, applied early

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different insecticide group next time, so the pest does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to integrated pest management](/pests/integrated-pest-management) explains how.

items: Strip and clean the trees fully after harvest.
Remove all fallen and dried berries from the ground.
Keep trees pruned and well fed.
Sample berries every few weeks from the start of ripening.

items.q: How big is the coffee berry borer?
items.a: About 1.5 mm long and black. You need a close look to see it.
Only when monitoring shows more than 2 percent of berries infested. Spray early, before the females go deep into the bean.
Taking every berry off the tree after harvest, and collecting the fallen ones. That leaves no berries to carry the beetles over.
